title: ase.ga moved to external project
body:
The `ase.ga` package now lives at https://dtu-energy.github.io/ase-ga/ , maintained by @stly.

This MR adds "deprecated placeholders" for all the `ase.ga` modules so we import everything from this project, removing the old modules.  We can remove these placeholders in the future.  We link to the new ase-ga project in different places.

We should also add an "ASE Ecosystem" description and link to ase-ga.

# Checklist: `x` (done) or `~` (irrelevant)

- [ ] [I am familiar with **ASE's contribution guidelines.**](https://ase-lib.org/development/contribute.html)
- [ ] [**Doc strings** in code changed in this MR are up to date.](https://ase-lib.org/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code)
- [ ] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://ase-lib.org/development/tests.html)
- [ ] [**Changes** have been added in `changelog.d` using `scriv`.](https://ase-lib.org/development/writing_changelog.html)
- [ ] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: askhl

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
@stly This MR aliases everything to the `ase_ga` package and has import errors/warnings to help people transition.

Do you have any comments, and would you like to add a description for the ASE Ecosystem page?  Is there anything else we should do to advertise the ase_ga project?

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
@stly Could you have a look at this please?  Maybe add an entry on the "ecosystem" page (can be separate MR or push to this branch)

For example it would be nice to know if this is removing anything (e.g. a tutorial) which *isn't* in ase-ga.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
@stly The ga tests will need maintenance due to some unclosed database connections that there are now warnings about.  Since ASE is no longer the preferred place for that, I am going to merge this, hence eliminating the need for those tests to be updated here.  Please feel free to follow up.

Please note that the ase_ga might break a little bit if/when we fix the database connection warnings, since it uses some private method of ase.db.

comments.author: stly
comments.body:
@askhl thank you for taking care of this. I transferred all the tutorials as well, so they should live with the ase-ga package.

I'll keep an eye out for the warnings, I'm not seeing them even when running the ase-ga tests with latest ASE commit. Are there any tricks I am missing?

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: In python 3.13 there are some database-closing-related warnings.  Basically we (somewhat unsurprisingly) had a habit of not closing database connections.
